title: What If Every Fly Vanished?
subject: fly

scenes.text: What if every fly vanished? Your chocolate goes first.
Cocoa trees are pollinated by midges, tiny flies a few millimetres long. Only about one flower in four hundred sets fruit.
A 2019 study of 105 food crops found flies visiting seventy-two percent of them.
Flies are nature's recyclers. Dead wood, rotting flesh and waste would pile up faster.
Birds, reptiles, amphibians, spiders and fish all eat flies. Their food chains would wobble.
Over a hundred and fifty thousand fly species exist. Losing them wouldn't end the world, but it would end chocolate.

description:
What if every fly vanished?
Cocoa depends on tiny midges, flies visit most food crops, and they recycle dead matter and feed countless animals.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Which animal would you want to see vanish, and which would you keep? What should we run through next?
